subject: Residency affirmation + access zones & KMS segmentation
messages:
From: Alan Choi <alan.choi@healthify.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: security@healthify.com
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Hosting residency confirmation + VPC controls (SIG follow-up)

Hi Aisha,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our security team has started the SIG questionnaire and flagged a few items where they need explicit confirmation:

1) Data residency — can you confirm which Redwood-hosted regions will store Healthify customer data by default (for US tenants)? We need the canonical region strings for our compliance docs (e.g., us-west-2, us-east-1).
2) VPC/private deployment — do you offer a Private (VPC) deployment for Dedicated customers? If so, what network controls are available for private link/peering and egress restrictions?
3) KMS/Key separation — for Private deployments can customer-managed keys be used such that keys and ciphertext never leave the customer KMS boundary?
4) Evidence — any diagrams, SOC 2 snapshots, or short runbook snippets we can attach to the questionnaire would be helpful.

Can your team provide short, certifiable statements for the SIG and a couple of supporting artifacts? We prefer separate technical attachments rather than long inline blocks in the questionnaire.

Best,
Alan

[Healthify — Security]

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alan Choi <alan.choi@healthify.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>, security@healthify.com
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 12:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Hosting residency confirmation + VPC controls (SIG follow-up)

Hi Alan,

Thanks — we can provide the confirmations and artifacts. Short answers up front, then we will follow with attachments: 

• Residency: For hosted (shared) tenants in the US we operate primary clusters in us-west-2 and us-east-1; customers can pin region preference per project. For Redwood Private (VPC) we support deployment into the customer region and the nodes remain in that region.
• Private/VPC: Yes — Redwood Private supports customer VPC peering and AWS PrivateLink. Network controls include enforceable egress rules, VPC endpoint-only access, and subnet-scoped routing for inference nodes.
• KMS: For Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS keys (CMKs). When configured, our runtime never stores plaintext model inputs or outputs outside encrypted volumes; keys remain in customer KMS and access is restricted by IAM roles and a hardware-backed key policy.

Ive looped in Marcus (platform infra) and Evelyn (compliance) to attach the network diagram, a short KMS partitioning note, and a SOC 2 snapshot. Expect a technical runbook and two attachments in a follow-up within 48 hours.

Next step: Marcus — can you produce a one-page network diagram and a 2-3 paragraph KMS access boundary note that we can sign off as Redwood statements? Evelyn, can you confirm if the SOC 2 snapshot is OK to share with Healthify?

Thanks,
Aisha

Aisha Rahman
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0132

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>, Alan Choi <alan.choi@healthify.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>, security@healthify.com
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 10:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Hosting residency confirmation + attachments

Aisha/Alan — attaching the artifacts per Aisha's note. Below are the technical excerpts you can paste into SIG answers and a note about what is claimable vs. operational detail.

--- Forwarded attachment stubs ---
[Attachment: redwood_network-segmentation-diagram.png (image/png) — diagram shows control plane separated from inference nodes; dedicated inference subnets; peering via AWS Transit Gateway or customer-managed VPC peering; PrivateLink endpoints for API fronting.]

[Attachment: redwood_kms-partitioning-notes.pdf (application/pdf) — 2 pages summarizing KMS usage: customer-managed CMKs supported for Redwood Private; envelope encryption used at rest; key access limited to customer IAM principals and a narrow Redwood runtime role; no plaintext key export; audit logs routed to customer CloudTrail when Private is deployed.]

[Attachment: redwood_public-soc2-snapshot.pdf (application/pdf) — 1-page SOC 2 scope summary (redacted) suitable for vendor security review.]

Technical excerpt for SIG/CAIQ answers (feel free to quote):
1) Data residency: "Redwood Inference offers hosted US regions (us-west-2, us-east-1). For Redwood Private, deployments are placed in the customer's selected region; persistent storage and inference compute remain within that region."
2) Network controls: "Redwood Private supports customer VPC peering or AWS PrivateLink. Customers can restrict egress by subnet-level route tables and security groups. Control-plane traffic can be restricted to management subnets and configured to use NAT or VPC endpoints per customer policy."
3) KMS/key separation: "When customer-managed KMS is selected for a Private deployment, encryption keys remain in the customer's KMS. Redwood uses envelope encryption and does not persist plaintext keys. Access is governed by customer key policies and IAM trust boundaries; CloudTrail audit events can be forwarded to the customer's account."

Note on phrasing: The SOC 2 snapshot is a vendor-facing summary; please do not attach internal SOC 2 audit evidence. If Healthify needs deeper evidence, we can proceed via an NDA and a vendor-facing evidence room.

Marcus Lin
Principal Platform Engineer — Serving Runtime
marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com

Thanks Aisha and Marcus — the attachments and excerpts are perfect and map cleanly to our SIG. A few quick clarifications before we mark items closed: 

• Can you confirm that when a customer requests Private deployment with CMK, the KMS keys are created in Healthify's account (not a Redwood-managed account)?
• For the network diagram: can you annotate where customer CloudTrail export points are configured and whether we can consume control-plane logs in our account?

If those are OK, well close the SIG items and upload the artifacts. Once closed, would you be able to sign the last page of our security questionnaire (DocuSign link below)?

DocuSign: https://docusign.com/XYZ-Healthify-Security-Questionnaire

Best,
Alan
